writing_intro: This is my daily writing practice. I write something every day, because writing is a skill I'm working to get better at, and right now I'm not a good writer.
Expect random pieces: things I learn while studying, short stories, and whatever's on my mind. Some will be rough. That's the point.

welcome.intro: I'm teaching myself electrical engineering and computer science from the ground up, while working full time. This homepage is where I show the work.
welcome.one_line_why: I've never finished anything I started. This is the one I finish.
goals: the first real milestone, and the one I'm working toward now.
the equivalent of MIT's 6-3 degree plus a master's: 54 courses and roughly 6,600 hours, from arithmetic and grammar up through systems, hardware and a capstone.
one lesson, one page and one project at a time.
whys: I've always been drawn to programming, but I never followed through. I've never finished anything I started, and that eats at me. This is the one I finish.
I want to stop feeling like the "dumb" one.
I couldn't hear until I was six and was in speech therapy until 8th grade. I never really learned to spell, so I stayed away from writing. Now I study the basics again and write every day, in public.

I spent years in fast food and package handling. I'm good at running a shift, but I've had gas in the tank I wasn't using. With AI moving this fast, I want to be someone who builds the future, not someone it replaces.
When my energy has nowhere to go, it turns into beating myself up. When it goes into something bigger, it comes back.
welcome.quote: If my fuel goes to my purpose, then my purpose is going to fill my fuel.
keep_score: Lessons and courses finished, counted from my study vault. The numbers on this site update themselves.
Writing every day, and publishing the pieces I'm proud of.
A skill ladder from student to principal engineer, scored by what I can actually do. These are benchmarks to measure myself against, not titles I'm chasing.
